content: It is not the critic who counts; not the man who points out how the strong man stumbles. The credit belongs to the man who is actually in the arena.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

Theodore Roosevelt understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: What authentic choice would you make right now if fear were completely off the table?
